title: Composite

act2.summary: a new node kind: a walking transfer

solutions.title: one RouteNode interface, one CompositeRouteNode base, no instanceof
solutions.tradeoff: A new node kind is one new file implementing RouteNode - totalMinutes never changes, and neither does CompositeRouteNode. The price: the total for one specific node no longer has one obvious place to read it from - it's whatever totalMinutes() resolves to, spread across however many classes the tree actually uses.

reviewFocus: Does totalMinutes' own body change at all between act 1 and act 2 on the solution route?
If a sixth node kind arrived, would CompositeRouteNode need to change?
Is Line and Journey both extending CompositeRouteNode the right call, or should Journey be allowed to do something a Line can't - and would that still fit one shared base class?
Would a plain recursive function over a discriminated union (a `kind` tag plus `children?`) be simpler than an interface and a class hierarchy, for a tree this shape?
